name: integrations
title: Integrations
summary: Claude Code and Codex get the official GitHub, Context7, and Convex plugins, and Claude can hand work to Codex.
day: Agents read and change your GitHub issues and pull requests, look up current library docs before they write code, and inspect your Convex deployments. With both AI plans, Claude hands a task or a review to Codex.
cost: Each plugin signs in once on each machine, and fleet doctor says how: a GitHub token for Claude, Context7 through its own sign-in or an API key, and Convex through its CLI. Codex's GitHub and Convex plugins use your ChatGPT sign-in. Convex starts off.
risk: The plugins act with the accounts you sign in with. Fleet removes only plugins that it installed, and keeps a plugin you turn off in your settings off.

workflows.name: GitHub
workflows.sentence: Agents read and change issues and pull requests through GitHub's official plugin.

workflows.name: Context7
workflows.sentence: Agents look up current library documentation through Context7.

workflows.name: Convex
workflows.sentence: Agents get Convex guidance and inspect the deployment of the project they work in.

workflows.name: Codex from Claude
workflows.sentence: Claude Code hands a task, a diagnosis, or a review to Codex through OpenAI's Codex plugin.

checks.say: Claude's GitHub plugin cannot reach GitHub. It reads a token from GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN in the environment that starts Claude Code. Create a fine-grained, read-only token on GitHub for the repositories you work in, export it in your shell profile, and start a new shell. You can export "$(gh auth token)" instead, but that puts your broad gh token into the environment of every agent you start. This check runs in fleet doctor's shell; an app that starts Claude Code with its own environment, such as T3 Code, needs the token there too. Fleet never stores the token.
Claude's Context7 plugin is not signed in. In Claude Code, run /mcp, choose plugin:context7:context7, and authenticate.

run: [ -n "$CONTEXT7_API_KEY" ] || codex mcp list 2>/dev/null | awk '$1 == "context7" { print $NF }' | grep -qx OAuth
checks.say: Codex cannot reach Context7. Run codex mcp login context7, or export CONTEXT7_API_KEY in your shell profile: Codex sends it to Context7 as a header and Fleet never writes it into config.toml.
Convex is not signed in on this machine. In a Convex project, run npx convex login. Each project then picks its own deployment, and agents should never point at a production deployment by default.
